claims.text: A predictive approach incorporating configurational disorder and local atomic-environment effects will identify low-phonon-thermal-conductivity HEAs more accurately than rule-of-mixtures or average-property models.
Configurational disorder contributes to phonon-scattering mechanisms that reduce heat transport in HEAs.
Local vibrational modes contribute to reduced heat transport in HEAs.
The relevant HEAs have random solid-solution structures.
The relevant HEAs are typically multicomponent transition-metal alloys.
The predictive model explicitly represents configurational disorder and local atomic environments.
The proposed approach is applicable from room temperature to approximately 800 K.
The proposed approach is applicable to bulk polycrystalline HEAs.
The proposed approach is applicable to alloys having at least four principal elements.
Atomic-scale disorder and local-environment variation enhance phonon scattering in HEAs.
Mass disorder produces complex phonon-scattering processes in HEAs.
Force-constant disorder produces complex phonon-scattering processes in HEAs.
Average-property models do not adequately represent phonon scattering caused by mass and force-constant disorder.
Representing disorder-driven phonon scattering will improve the accuracy of predicted low thermal conductivity.
The proposed approach will reduce phonon-thermal-conductivity prediction RMSE by at least 30% relative to rule-of-mixtures or average-property models.
The proposed approach does not apply to ordered intermetallics.
The proposed approach does not apply to nanostructured composites.
The magnitude of prediction improvement depends on the quality and diversity of the training data.
The magnitude of prediction improvement depends on the degree of alloy disorder.
Failure to achieve at least a 30% RMSE reduction across the tested HEAs would falsify the hypothesis.
